chains.title: FOXA1-dependent effect at a candidate TOX3 regulatory region
chains.element: Intronic CASC16 sequence annotated with an enhancer feature; the nearest ENCODE dELS cCRE is 38 bp away and does not overlap the variant.

links.claim: FOXA1 is a candidate because it has five MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant and is highly expressed there. Ref G is entered as a provisional direction only to make this chain testable; no QBiC-SELEX result or allele-specific evidence supports ref over alt, so the actual binding direction is unknown. FOXA1 is prioritized among the many bound TFs because its MCF-7 occupancy is repeatedly reported in this context.
The site is intronic in CASC16 and has an enhancer-feature annotation, but the nearby ENCODE dELS cCRE does not overlap it; enhancer activity at the variant has not been functionally demonstrated.

TOX3 is a candidate target because its TSS is 17.6 kb away, but no evidence links this site to TOX3 regulation. No significant GTEx eQTL is reported for this variant, including in breast mammary tissue.
MCF-7 is a relevant context for this candidate because FOXA1 occupancy over the variant and high FOXA1 expression are reported there.
TOX3 has breast-cancer gene-level context, but the supplied literature concerns other variants or candidate loci and does not establish a role for rs56007086 in breast cancer.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 occupancy at the site should be detectable if this chain is correct; ref is the provisional test direction, not an evidence-supported result.
An isogenic G-to-A edit should alter TOX3 expression in MCF-7, and the effect should be reduced by FOXA1 depletion or disruption of FOXA1 binding at the site.
falsified_if: A sensitive allele-specific assay finds no FOXA1 occupancy difference or finds greater occupancy with alt A, and isogenic editing produces no FOXA1-dependent change in TOX3 expression.
